sourceItems.title: International uncertainty drives 2Q25 memory contract-price upgrades
normalizedClaims: Tariff/international uncertainty triggered inventory building and stronger DRAM/NAND transaction momentum; TrendForce raised Q2 contract-price expectations but warned the demand impulse might be front-loaded.

sourceItems.title: Rising Demand and EOL Plans Drive Strong DDR4 Contract Price Hikes in 2Q25
normalizedClaims: Server DDR4 contract prices were forecast +18-23% QoQ and PC DDR4 +13-18%, upgraded sharply because major suppliers were reducing DDR4 output/EOL while CSP and tariff-frontloaded demand increased procurement.

sourceItems.title: DRAM Market Bulletin - Jun. 25, 2025
normalizedClaims: DDR4/LPDDR4 phase-out was causing supply shortages and price jumps; legacy capacity remained tight even as spot demand fluctuated.

sourceItems.title: Niche DRAM Price Jun. 2025
normalizedClaims: DDR4 EOL news triggered aggressive procurement; spot/contract prices for DDR4 8/16Gb rose sharply, some contract prices >20% MoM, with demand still exceeding available supply.

sourceItems.title: ABB Q1 2025 results
normalizedClaims: Group orders +5% comparable; Electrification orders +2% comparable with book-to-bill 1.15 and backlog at an all-time-high $8.2bn.

sourceItems.title: GE Vernova Q1 2025 results
normalizedClaims: Orders $10.2bn +8% organically, Power equipment +43%; backlog grew $4.4bn sequentially; 29GW gas equipment in backlog plus 21GW slot reservations.

sourceItems.title: Auto companies in full panic over rare-earths bottleneck
normalizedClaims: China's April export curbs created an acute magnet bottleneck; some European auto suppliers/plants faced stoppages and urgent sourcing inquiries.

sourceItems.title: China rare earth magnet shipments halve in May due to export curbs
normalizedClaims: May rare-earth magnet exports fell 52.9% MoM and 74% YoY to the lowest since Feb 2020 after April export curbs; licensing delays constrained shipments.

sourceItems.title: China installation rush expected to lift 2Q25 PV-chain prices
normalizedClaims: Distributed-PV installation rush was expected to support Q2 wafer/cell/module demand and prices, but TrendForce explicitly expected demand/pricing to weaken after the rush into Q3.

sourceItems.title: Losses, pricing reform in focus at Shanghai solar conference
normalizedClaims: Chinese solar manufacturers were posting major losses as overcapacity pushed prices below production costs; May output fell 7% and June cuts were expected despite the installation rush and pricing reform.
observedChanges: installation boom does not translate to producer margins

sourceItems.title: 2025年5月全国新增建档立卡新能源发电项目情况
normalizedClaims: NEA recorded 4,875 new PV projects (excluding household PV) in May, confirming unusually intense pre-reform project activity.

sourceItems.title: 2025年4月中国采购经理指数运行情况
normalizedClaims: April manufacturing PMI fell to 49.0; production 49.8 and new orders 49.2, with new export orders 44.7/42.2 range depending series, showing tariff-related demand shock.

sourceItems.title: 2025年5月中国采购经理指数运行情况
normalizedClaims: May manufacturing PMI improved to 49.5 but remained below 50; production recovered while new orders remained below the expansion threshold.

sourceItems.title: 2025年6月中国采购经理指数运行情况
normalizedClaims: June manufacturing PMI improved to 49.7; production 51.0 and new orders 50.2, but overall PMI remained below 50.

sourceItems.title: 2025年4月份工业生产者出厂价格同比下降2.7%
normalizedClaims: April PPI -2.7% YoY and -0.4% MoM; broad producer deflation persisted while non-ferrous material/wire purchase prices rose 8.5% YoY.

sourceItems.title: 2025年5月份工业生产者出厂价格同比下降3.3%
normalizedClaims: May PPI -3.3% YoY and -0.4% MoM; producer deflation deepened, while non-ferrous purchase prices remained +4.6% YoY.

eventClusters.statement: Q2 memory demand initially accelerated partly because of tariff/inventory front-loading, but by June a more structural DDR4 mechanism was visible: supplier EOL/output reductions plus CSP/server demand drove repeated price upgrades and shortages.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: All physical evidence shares one specialist origin and part of Q2 demand is tariff front-loading. Deep research must distinguish direct chip pricing power from inventory/speculative exposure.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Which A-share memory company had a direct, observable earnings-conversion bridge from DDR4 price/supply changes before Q2 ended?

eventClusters.statement: Global power/electrification equipment demand stayed structurally strong: ABB Electrification backlog reached an all-time high and GE Vernova reported accelerating Power equipment orders and sequential backlog growth.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: The theme is increasingly known; selection requires a company-level realized/quantitative earnings bridge, not backlog proxy alone.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Which A-share power-equipment name converts the global order cycle into near-term earnings with favorable timing and asymmetry?

eventClusters.statement: China's April rare-earth export controls became a real physical bottleneck by June: magnet exports collapsed and auto suppliers warned of production stoppages.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Export restrictions can help upstream scarcity while hurting export-dependent magnet producers. Company incidence must be verified.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Does any A-share upstream or magnet company have a direct price/volume earnings bridge rather than a generic policy label?

eventClusters.statement: China's PV installation rush created extraordinary Q2 project activity and temporary wafer/cell/module price support, but by June manufacturing overcapacity and losses persisted and output cuts began. Installation volume and manufacturer profit moved in opposite directions.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Huge installations do not make module manufacturers winners. Deep research must map which parts capture installation volume without commodity-manufacturing losses.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Is there a profitable A-share expression of the rush—such as inverter/grid equipment—after excluding loss-making module capacity?

eventClusters.statement: China manufacturing fell back into contraction in April after tariff escalation and only partially recovered by June.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Useful regime/context evidence but not a narrow long opportunity.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Should this remain a contradiction/timing filter rather than a standalone selection?

eventClusters.statement: Producer-price deflation deepened through May despite pockets of non-ferrous input inflation.
eventClusters.contradictionSearchNotes: Broad PPI weakness identifies margin pressure but not a specific winner.
eventClusters.researchQuestion: Does any narrow value-chain spread emerge, or is this macro context only?
